exercise.artifact: http.cap from Wireshark SampleCaptures (exact URL in resource 8); Zeek quickstart.pcap linked in resource 7.
steps: Open http.cap; apply http.request; select one request and record source/destination IP, method, Host and URI.
Follow its TCP stream; record response status and distinguish client/server bytes. Note the stream filter.
Run tshark -r http.cap -Y http.request -T fields -E header=y -e ip.src -e ip.dst -e http.request.method -e http.host -e http.request.uri ; compare selected GUI values.
In a new directory run zeek -r /path/to/quickstart.pcap LogAscii::use_json=T ; join http.log to weird.log using uid.
exercise.assessment: GUI request values must match a TShark row; record stream response evidence. Zeek guide expects GET and WEIRD requests; the WEIRD uid joins unknown_HTTP_method. Do not compare generated UID strings to the guide literally.

steps: For prepared ffufme: open one lesson, capture its request into Burp Repeater and record the baseline response.
Modify one input; compare status, body length/content and headers; reproduce the same request using curl.
Choose a small local wordlist and one FUZZ marker; measure a nonexistent-input baseline before selecting -fs or -fc; bound the run with -maxtime.

exercise.assessment: Explain each changed request byte and cite corresponding response evidence; do not treat status alone or an ffuf match as proof. Reconstructed curl request must preserve intended method/path/cookie/header/body.

offline_paper_alternative.artifact_name: web-refresher-paper.txt (synthetic teaching data, not real portal/challenge evidence)
offline_paper_alternative.request:
GET /product?productId=1 HTTP/1.1
Host: lab.example
Cookie: session=demo
tasks: Write a curl command preserving Host, cookie and query, then a variant changing only productId.
Explain what each result suggests and what it does not prove; propose one next manual test.
Write an ffuf command using a three-line local wordlist [1,999999,abc], marker in the productId value, -fs 120 and -maxtime 30. Predict retained rows for these synthetic observations.
Explain what -c versus -b does and why curl can exit successfully while the HTTP response is 404.
answer_checks: One valid reconstruction: curl -H "Cookie: session=demo" "http://lab.example/product?productId=1" (paper only; lab.example is a placeholder).
Use ffuf -w ids.txt -u "http://lab.example/product?productId=FUZZ" -fs 120 -maxtime 30. 1 and abc survive the size filter; neither is automatically a vulnerability.
Error suggests type handling and potential information disclosure; existence of exploitable injection is not established.
-c writes cookie jar, -b reads it; curl transfer success is distinct from server status unless failure options are requested.

family_rationales: Burp/curl/ffuf form one inspect-replay-enumerate workflow; Feroxbuster/Gobuster/Katana stay reference-only to avoid repeating discovery introductions.
SQLmap and jwt_tool are vulnerability-specific lookups after identifying relevant SQL/JWT evidence; PayloadsAllTheThings remains indexed reference, not cover-to-cover reading.
Nmap gets a short state/service refresher; RustScan/Legion repeat reconnaissance setup, and Impacket/Metasploit/Hydra require a specific service/target, so retain their exact approved references.

CAN utilities/cannelloni and RTP tools need matching bus/media artifacts; wireless Aircrack/hcxtools need captures and protocol prerequisites. Keep references rather than requiring hardware/live work on a plane.
Subfinder is the sole OSINT entry in this lane and needs network-backed passive sources; explicitly reference-only.
tcpdump and Zui overlap the selected packet workflow; retain their tool-specific references. OpenVPN setup and Chrome DevTools remain utility lookups.

Community manual tools are usable; Professional scanner, Collaborator, full Intruder and saved project files must not be implied by the training plan. Supplemental ffufme/Docker home practice does not expand event approval.
